translations.text: This is the Synodos of Clement, written by Peter, the disciple and chief of the apostles, who spoke about our Lord Jesus Christ.
Clement said, on the authority of Peter, chief of the apostles and disciple of our Lord Christ:
He said to me, “My son Clement, do not baptize anyone for bribes or for a fixed payment for baptism.
Whoever accepts bribes for baptism at a fixed price is excommunicated and cursed by my mouth—I, Peter, the least of the apostles. Let his portion be with Simon the sorcerer and Judas the wicked.

My son, do not sell the gift of priesthood and the grace of the Holy Spirit for a price. Do not bargain over the priesthood, and do not accept payment for it, either before you give the blessing or afterward, except as a blessing.

Whoever gives or receives bribes for the priesthood has no priesthood. He is excommunicated by me, Peter, with the excommunication with which I excommunicated Simon the sorcerer. Let his portion be with Judas the rebellious, and let his soul be far from the presence of God, as the devil is far from his former rank.
My son, forgive whoever sins against you seventy times seven, as our Lord commanded in the holy Gospel.

Receive whoever repents of his sin. Have mercy on whoever has sinned, take him by the hand and raise him up, and admonish him. Visit the sick, go to the prisoners, feed the hungry, give drink to the thirsty, and clothe the naked.

Be steadfast in the faith and struggle for it with the uprightness that is fitting. Listen to the holy Scriptures of God, for those who hold firmly to the faith and struggle for it will inherit the kingdom of heaven.

My son, forgive so that you may be forgiven, and do not judge so that you may not be judged. If you have been entrusted with authority appointed by God and judge people, judge with justice and uprightness, as our law declares. Fight with an iron sword against unbelievers and rebels who do not believe in Christ, and sharpen your sword for the perfect faith. Do not show partiality or accept bribes in judgment. Let the rich and the poor be alike before you.

Have mercy on the orphan and provide for the widow. Protect the virgins and strengthen them. Do not give Satan a way to attack you, but drive away his accursed power through fasting, prayer, and keeping watch at night. Let almsgiving be your distinguishing sign, your house, and your dwelling. Protect the children of baptism and the faith.
Do not accept the profession of faith of a man who has not been baptized.

If you see a poor priest, help him by giving him alms, and do not leave him to [?] among the foolish people. Do likewise for all the messengers of God. If you have a blessing, give it to the children of baptism.

Devote yourself earnestly to building churches, monasteries, and convents, which are a dwelling for those oppressed in the world and for the poor. Build houses of God with bright lights, such as wax candles and lamps. Whoever does this, God will approve his deeds and his final outcome.
Fast on Wednesday and Friday all the days of your life.

Let Sunday be a festival. No work is to be done on it except reading the Scriptures concerning the Godhead. Whoever transgresses this is excommunicated and cursed by the three names of God: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

Do not drive a poor person away from the door of your dwelling. Do not mock him, reject him, or belittle him. Rather, let your generosity of heart lead you to comfort him and make him glad, so that God may make you glad. Seat him with you at your table, and give him drink from the cup from which you drink. Do not boast over him, for King Nebuchadnezzar boasted and was destroyed, and the wrath of God overtook him.

Do not exalt yourself before a king or act for show in his house. Do not boast over him about your good deeds. Rather, when you do every good deed and fulfill every commandment, say, ‘I am a worthless servant,’ as our Lord said in the book of life, for you will not be saved by the abundance of your evil deeds.
Do not accumulate gold and silver except what you distribute for the benefit of believers.

Give abundant peace to the children of the faithful, and praise the upright priest who knows God and acts according to his law. Beware of Satan’s deception, for he deceived Simon the sorcerer after he became a disciple of my brother Philip and after many divine miracles had appeared through his hands. The cause of his error was that he sought priestly ordination and the gift of the Holy Spirit from me through scheming. Our Lord told me that he was deceitful and a thief, and I drove him away from me. This led to his destruction.
My son, honor the elders, hold them in esteem, and listen to their words. Do not ridicule anyone because of his sin, but rebuke him, instruct him, and gently turn him toward the fear of God.
Instruct kings in righteousness and rebuke them for their evil conduct. Do not neglect God’s holy gifts on any day, for offering the sacrifice prevents [?].

Commemorate the dead on the third day, the seventh, the twelfth, the thirtieth, the fortieth, and the sixtieth. Know, my son, that on the fortieth day after the deceased’s passing, the soul of a baptized sinner stands before Christ. He is repaid according to his conduct, and they punish him according to what he has done.

Anoint anyone who desires baptism with the oil of gladness before you baptize him in water. After baptism, seal him with the divine oil that I gave you. This is the oil of chrism, through which everything is brought to completion. Let the faithful stand on their feet to listen to the holy, divine Scriptures.
Do not receive the holy gifts without having purified yourself and fasted.
Pray in the morning, at the third hour of the day, and in the evening, for these three prayers are required of all priests. Let the laypeople pray at dawn and in the evening.

Those who are able and seek a greater measure of divine grace should pray as we prescribed in the Book of Church Order. For Christ my God taught me, and I tell you, my son Clement, that they ought to pray at the first hour of the day, at the third hour, at the sixth hour, at the ninth hour, in the evening, at bedtime, and at midnight.
I, Peter, command the faithful to rest from their work and their occupations on the feast days of the martyrs.

I warn them against wicked drunkenness, attending theatrical performances, and singing in the streets. They must not eat what an unbaptized person has slaughtered, for God has abolished the sacrifices of the Jews and of foreign nations.

We command them not to eat the unleavened bread of the Jews or anything from their sacrifices. They must not give their own in marriage to them or marry anyone from among them. Anyone among them who believes and is baptized must stand at the church door for forty days and eat nothing but dry bread.

If he does this, let him approach God’s sanctuary after they have tested his faith, and let them pierce his ear. Let them feed him the offering of the faithful, and especially the flesh of the holy animal that appeared to me in a shining cloth that descended upon me in the city of Joppa, for it is holy among all animals.

When you wish to sleep, believer, make the sign of the cross over your face and your whole body. If you wish to set out on a journey, receive a blessing from the bones of the martyrs before you depart.

Priest, do not offer fat or flesh on the altar. Do not place anything on the altar except pure bread of fine flour, of which he said, “It is my body,” for God called it heavenly bread; and nothing from the [?] except grape juice, for God called it the water of life; and fresh ears from the wheat crop when it ripens. You are not permitted to bring anything else as an offering. A priest must not offer wine on the altar without adding water, for our Lord Christ said, “I am the water of life.”

Concerning the observance of festivals. Keep a festival during the days of Christ’s sufferings, his sorrow, and his crucifixion. During those days, join sorrow and joy together. Let there be sorrow because of his endurance in affliction, and joy because your salvation comes through Christ’s suffering.
The feast of Easter is greater and more honored than all the festivals. Let there be no sorrow in it, but only joy.
Commemorate your dead in the liturgy at all times, for this greatly benefits them and brings them near to our Lord Christ.
Celebrate the feast of Easter at its completion, on the Sunday that comes after Passover. This is the day of the resurrection of our Lord Christ from the tomb.

Celebrate a feast seven days after his resurrection, on New Sunday, for on that day he came to us, the assembly of the Twelve, after his resurrection from the dead, while we were gathered in the upper room in Zion with the doors shut. On that day Thomas found him and touched with his hand the place of the spear wound in the side of our Lord Christ and the places of the nails, until he burned the tips of his fingers. Our God renewed them and restored them to life, and said to him, “Do not doubt, Thomas, but believe.”

Celebrate the feast of his ascension into heaven and the feast of the descent of the Holy Spirit upon us apostles. For he descended from heaven upon our mouths like tongues of fire and taught us things that we did not know, had not heard before then, and had not understood. This was after Christ’s ascension into heaven, from which he had not departed, in a chariot of light from the Mount of Olives, forty days after his resurrection.

Celebrate a feast at the time of her annunciation, for the Gentiles celebrated it before you as a feast for their gods. But you are to make it a feast for the Mother of Light, as the chosen man of God, Paul, commanded.
Celebrate all the feasts that we commanded you in the Book of Church Order.

Know, my son, concerning incense with [?], for [?] is the great incense that they burn before God. Our Lady, the Mother of Light, told me and gave me some of it. It is what the Magi brought as a gift. Myrrh, however, is to be used for embalming the bodies of priests so that they do not decay. They are not to bury them in the earth, but halfway above the earth.
My son, keep my commandment as Joshua son of Nun kept the commandment of my brother Moses.

Concerning the consecration of the tabot. Consecrate every tabot of the law and seal it with the seal of God, which is chrism, the oil of gladness. Seven priests are to be with you when you consecrate it, for they are our successors. Seal the tabots and the altars with the seal of God, so that the glory of God may be found wherever they celebrate the consecration upon them. Seal everyone who is baptized with this holy oil. Through it they will receive priesthood and kingship, and prophecy will abound through the anointing with chrism and through its glory.

If anyone seals himself with this holy oil, which I, Peter, the least of the apostles, give you, without being sealed by a priest authorized to do so, let them seize him. I have authorized them to kill him.

If anyone drinks some of it for his healing, let him be banished to a place from which he will not return. Any layperson who dares to carry it without knowing is to be expelled from the church of God for seven years.
If he carries it knowingly, let them strike him with one hundred and fifty-three lashes, and let him remain outside the church for ten years.
If a priest anoints someone who has not been baptized with this oil, let him be removed from his office.
If a priest takes this oil to someone who is not a priest, let him be removed from his office.
If a priest carries this oil, let him recite the psalm of David the prophet, who prophesied concerning this oil, until he sets it down from his hands.
If anyone takes the priesthood for himself without receiving it from the chief priest, let him be expelled from the church of God.

Concerning the order of the altar. Let them consecrate the offering upon an altar sealed with chrism, on the first occasion when the chief priests and priests assemble together with all the deacons, so that there may be honor and joy. Likewise on Sabbaths and feast days. Let them read the Gospel of John over the altar, for he is the one who speaks of the Godhead.

In every sanctuary there are to be two altars: one that they carry from place to place, like the stone of the children of Israel in the wilderness, which they carried from place to place; and another that they do not move from its place.

If the altar that is not moved is broken, or people move it from the place where it was consecrated, know that its holiness has departed from it, just as the holiness of the children of Israel departed from his offspring. They must consecrate it again.

If one of the faithful is taken captive, or goes and joins the Gentiles, eats their food, has contact with them and they with him, and is defiled by them, and then returns to his country from his captivity, they must baptize him again.

If a layperson enters the holy altar of God during the consecration, seeking greater honor than his fellow, they must excommunicate him. He must stand outside the church for seven years and show people his repentance.

If a layperson insults a priest or curses him, he must be banished from the cities of God and his churches to the land of rebels. If he seeks refuge at the altar of God and takes hold of the vestments, the priest must prescribe twelve years of fasting for him and perform over him the anointing for the forgiveness of sins.

If a man or woman among the faithful eats any of what is offered, that person must be banished from the church of God until death, if this was done out of contempt. If it was done without knowledge, that person must fast for twelve full years. They must give the church double that person's possessions. That person must not give orders but must be put to work.

If a man among the faithful enters inside the curtain of the altar, stretches out his hand against a priest, and strikes him, they must cut off his hand for his insolence toward the priesthood of God.
If a man among the faithful has committed many sins and wishes to refrain from them, he must disclose them to the priests and to those learned in the Scriptures of God.

Concerning priestly vestments. Priestly vestments must be different from the clothing of laypeople. The priest's garment should be loose, without folds, and its [?] should be wide at the bottom. His garment must be like this, and its upper part must be rounded, for this represents the binding of the feet of our Lord Christ. He must uncover his hands with a cord.

The priest must wear a cloth like a neckband over his shoulders, for it represents the cord they placed around the neck of our Lord Christ when they dragged him to Pilate's courtyard. His belt must be broad and made of leather.
The priest must read the Psalms of David by day and the Praises of the Prophets by night, for through this they will be girded with two swords.

I tell you, my son Clement, and those who share your rank, to judge between the faithful and give them appropriate commands according to what the Holy Spirit has shown you, who brings [?] to completion. Whoever rebels and leads others astray is cursed until the day of judgment, when he will stand before Christ.
Know, my son, that everything I have commanded you, I have commanded you by God's command.
With his own hand he wrote this command for me and gave it to me on the Mount of Olives on the day of his ascension into his glory. Amen.
